key_insight: How patient records are grouped during EHR model pretraining can materially improve downstream clinical prediction, even without changing the model architecture or adding data.
clinical_relevance: A better pretraining sequence format may help foundation models produce more accurate risk predictions across common hospital datasets and tasks.
method: Compared a global-stream pretraining baseline against alternative ways of composing patient sequences.
Controlled how much each patient trajectory contributes to training windows.
Evaluated effects on multiple clinical prediction benchmarks under the same training recipe.
evidence_signal: Across four MIMIC-IV v2.2 tasks and four additional evaluation settings, the best method improved macro AUROC, AUPRC, F1, and balanced accuracy, including gains of 9.3% in F1 and 2.7% in AUPRC.
watch_item: Results are benchmark-specific, so real-world benefit may depend on the dataset, task mix, and how sequences are constructed in deployment.
paper_title: Sequence Composition in EHR Foundation Model Pretraining
